gen-amatic-sc-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight reads like a plain sans with its curve tails pulled back and ascenders barely rising. Amatic SC adds a rustic, pen-and-paper wobble up top, and that handwritten-versus-tidy split is what makes this pairing memorable.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-julius-sans-one: Thin toothpaste-line strokes with terminals that stop far from the stem give Amatic SC its quirky, hand-drawn look. Julius Sans One answers with sparse, spacious sans-serif letters.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads as a text serif with a large x-height and curves that stay open, classic and editorial. And Amatic SC, with horizontal bars as heavy as its stems, brings a rustic hand-lettered jolt above it.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-karla: Quirky and rustic, Amatic SC draws its heading in plain stitched-thread outlines, while Karla below has a gaping c and a stocky tall middle band. Handwritten meets sans, and that gap is the whole appeal.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-kedebideri: Amatic SC draws every stroke at a single thickness, like squeezed toothpaste. Kedebideri below has a skyward x-height and rounded, inviting letters, so the plain sans body keeps the hand-drawn heading from running away with the page.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-khula: Khula reads as a modern sans-serif, its tall midsection and open-mouthed curves making text feel straightforward and unfussy. Amatic SC above has no visible gap between its up and side strokes, which makes the two a fun mismatch.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-krub: Amatic SC brings rustic, quirky handwriting, even its w drawn without thick or thin strokes. Krub follows in a plain sans with a pronounced x-height and curves that leave their loops unfinished, giving the heading a grounded partner.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-kufam: Kufam reads like neon tubing, one track width with generous e openings and ascenders that hardly show. Amatic SC sits above it in rustic handwriting, so the heading feels sketched while the text beneath feels cleanly drawn.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-lexend: Lexend reads big and friendly, with oversized lowercase and open jaws on every curve. Lexend would carry a long passage in a sans that never crowds, while Amatic SC adds its handwritten quirk only at the top.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-lexend-deca: Amatic SC has a rustic, hand-drawn stroke with terminals that stop far from the stem. But Lexend Deca keeps a long passage smooth, its plain sans line never swelling and its small capitals tucked beside big lowercase.
